title: surge-zeroshot: code, frozen splits, evaluation protocol and trained models for "Storm surge forecasts from a global tide-gauge network"
description:
Archived release of the repository that accompanies the manuscript Storm surge forecasts from a global tide-gauge network (Heshan Chen and Andrew Kruczkiewicz, 2026). One recurrent neural network trained on 760 quality-screened tide gauges from the GESLA-3 archive, with open atmospheric forcing from the Open-Meteo historical archive, forecasts storm surge 1 to 48 hours ahead at gauges and whole regions that were never used in training.

The release holds the dataset recipe, the pre-registered split files (deployment split, four leave-region-out rotations, scaling ladder, composition and intervention experiments), the continuous-window evaluation protocol and its scripts, per-gauge evaluation tables and training logs, the sampled GEFSv12 reforecast forcing at the test gauges, the figure scripts and figures of record, and the trained model checkpoints (deployment model, gauge-free variant, rotation, ladder, composition and matched-update models). Two audit gates (scripts/verify_numbers_cont.py, 168 checks, and scripts/verify_numbers.py, 69 checks) assert every number quoted in the manuscript and in the July 2026 preprint directly from the committed artifacts. NUMBERS.md maps each claim to its artifact and script.

GESLA-3 and the Open-Meteo archive are open data; no registered product is required anywhere in the forecasting pipeline. Third-party datasets retain their own licences.
